title: 3.1 Pairs of Lines and Angles

icans: I can identify parallel lines, skew lines, and parallel planes.
I can use the Parallel and Perpendicular Postulates.
I can identify corresponding, alternate interior, alternate exterior, and consecutive interior angles.

vocab: lines that do not ____________ and are not coplanar
a line that _____________ two or more coplanar lines at different points

blocks.p: Draw a transversal across two lines of your notebook paper. Number the angles like the diagram on the TV and measure them.
Which pairs have the same measure?

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

blocks.stem:
Use the box.
a.  Name a line parallel to line AB.
b.  Name a line skew to line AB.
c.  Name a plane parallel to plane ABCD.

notes: Parallel Postulate: if there is a line and a point not on the line, then there is exactly _______________ line through the point parallel to the given line. (The Perpendicular Postulate says the same about perpendicular lines.)

blocks.stem: Point P is not on line ℓ. How many lines through P are parallel to ℓ? How many are perpendicular to ℓ?

notes: Corresponding angles are in the _______________ position at each intersection. Alternate interior angles lie between the two lines on _______________ sides of the transversal.

blocks.stem:

a.  Name all pairs of corresponding angles.
b.  Name both pairs of alternate interior angles.

notes: Alternate exterior angles lie _______________ the two lines on opposite sides of the transversal. Consecutive interior angles lie between the two lines on the _______________ side of the transversal.
